items.title: Henry "Jack" Palmer Interview
items.q: Mr. Livingston got it over in New York... Mr. Livingston is a very good business.

ctx.x: President Harry Gray, he was with the band, uh, at that time. And, uh, Frazier, uh, when I, oh, they had, oh, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I, I was the biggest Duke waiting by this. I came out of New York from the Black Fleet High Flyers. I came out of the White and Black River, I had 11 pieces of bands then. Duke didn't have but five. Well, he had a big band then, but I knew Duke when he had five pieces. I knew Basie when he was…
Did you play much in Chicago in the late 20s? No. I didn't do much playing here. I came came here at the hospital. But I think you know Jerome Carrington? He was the first musician I met.
